title.narrative: International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) Strategic Partnership Framework 2022-2026

description.narrative: The Australia - International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) Strategic Partnership Framework (SPF) sets the objectives and obligations for the partnership. It outlines the parameters for Australia's global funding, and the requirements for any subsidiary arrangements that will direct funding to specific crises/programmes.

description.narrative:
Australia’s funding to the International Committee of the Red Cross
In 2023, Australia’s core funding ($27.5 million) to the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) contributed to ICRC assisting 11.5 million people affected by conflict in more than 27 countries around the world. Our unearmarked contribution gave the ICRC operational flexibility to respond to escalations in conflict, such as in Armenia and Azerbaijan, and address humanitarian needs in many underfunded crises, including in Ethiopia which faced multiple emergencies in 2023. The ICRC’s neutral, impartial and independent approach remained a hallmark of its work, enabling it to gain trust, acceptance and access in highly complex and dangerous settings. This in turn enabled ICRC to reach people that few or no other actors could. Australia’s flexible funding also supported the ICRC to continue engaging with influential actors to promote international humanitarian law and influence policies affecting key issues of humanitarian concern.

In 2024, Australia’s core funding to the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) supported humanitarian operations in over 15 countries and regional contexts, helping to assist more than 5.8 million people affected by conflict around the world. ‍ Australia’s unearmarked contribution enabled the ICRC to rapidly respond to escalations in conflict and sustain operations in protracted crises such as in Yemen. The ICRC’s role as an independent, impartial and neutral intermediary continued to facilitate access to vulnerable populations in hard-to-reach and high-risk environments. ‍ Through Australia’s support, the ICRC improved access to clean water and sanitation, delivered income-generating assistance, and supported livelihood recovery and resilience across conflict-affected communities. Australia’s flexible funding also enabled the ICRC to strengthen engagement with influential actors and parties to conflict to promote adherence to and respect for international humanitarian law.
